title: Flow Canvas timeline grows unbounded, snapshots full unsanitized variables per step, and patches by mapping the whole array
existing_state: Every step that enters 'running' appends a TimelineEntry carrying a FULL snapshot of all current variables (FlowCanvas/src/stores/messageBridge.ts:250-271), with no cap and none of the sanitization the iteration log applies (iterationSlice.ts:12-32 strips heavy _outputwindow/_output keys and truncates strings at 2000 chars; the host-tunable iterationHistoryCap at iterationSlice.ts:8 has no timeline equivalent). Each new generation of variable values arrives as fresh objects from the JSON message, so timeline entries genuinely retain them: a loop over 100 hosts with multi-KB ${_output} values retains every generation until the next run or canvas close. Mechanically it is also quadratic: addTimelineEntry spreads the whole entries array per append (timelineSlice.ts:35-42) and updateTimelineEntry maps the entire array on every step completion (timelineSlice.ts:44-50). Entries accumulate whether or not the Timeline panel is open.
recommendation: In messageBridge.ts:253-262, run the variables snapshot through the same sanitizer iterationSlice uses (export sanitizeVars or a shared util) before storing. Add a cap to timelineEntries (reuse iterationHistoryCap or a sibling setting; drop oldest). Replace the full-array map in updateTimelineEntry with a reverse indexOf for the newest open entry for that nodeId and replace by index; skip snapshot capture entirely while the Timeline panel has never been opened to make it free by default.
user_benefit: Long, loop-heavy multi-host runs stop bloating WebView2 memory by tens-to-hundreds of MB and stop adding per-step array-copy cost; the canvas stays responsive across a full workday session.

evidence.note: full variables snapshot per 'running' event, unsanitized
unbounded append (array spread) + whole-array map per completion
